Severe Flooding Hits Banking Sector Sites Across Malaysia

Severe flooding has inundated several banking sector sites across Malaysia, disrupting operations and affecting hundreds of employees. The ongoing deluge, triggered by relentless monsoon rains since early this week, has particularly impacted branches and administrative offices of firms such as Nusantara Finance Holdings and Unity Bank Group in the states of Selangor and Pahang.

Banking premises in low-lying areas have experienced significant water ingress, with some facilities reporting floodwaters reaching desk height. “Our main branch in Temerloh is currently inaccessible, and staff safety is our top concern,” said Farid Azman, spokesperson for Nusantara Finance Holdings. “We have activated emergency protocols and are monitoring the situation closely.”

According to the Malaysian Banking Workers’ Union, over 600 employees have been advised to stay home as a precaution. “Our members are reporting anxiety over lost workdays and potential property damage,” union president Noraini Ismail stated. “We urge all banks to prioritize staff welfare and provide clear communication during this crisis.”

Automated teller machines and safe deposit vaults at several affected branches have been submerged, raising concerns about equipment damage and document security. The Association of Malaysian Banks has called on its members to conduct immediate risk assessments and review disaster recovery plans.

With rainfall forecast to continue over the coming days, banking firms are bracing for further operational challenges. “Our disaster response teams remain on high alert, and we are exploring all options to maintain essential services,” said Suresh Tan, head of operations at Unity Bank Group. “The safety of our people and the security of client assets are our priorities as this situation unfolds.”
